body:
**Scope:** root project (`.`) only: `DECISIONS.md` and `specs/15-board-api.md`. No code.

**Goal:** settle the model in writing so the code tasks can be built and reviewed against it.

**Add D-87 to the end of `DECISIONS.md`** (same short form as the others), saying:

1. A **milestone** is a planned release. A **feature** is a capability of the product. Both are records at the Solace root, kept by the task server, which is their only writer. They are not tasks (D-25) and have no column, runs, scope or workflow.
2. Links are optional. A task has at most one feature and at most one milestone. A feature has an optional *target* milestone. A task given a feature with no milestone of its own takes the feature's milestone; after that the two can differ. A feature appears in every milestone that holds one of its tasks.
3. Tasks gain `feature`, `milestone`, `dependsOn` (task ids), `closedTime` (when the task first reached a final column; never cleared) and `archivedTime` (when the task was archived; null otherwise). How a task is archived, and how the board hides it, is decided later.
4. `feature` and `milestone` can be changed on a task in a final column. Other edits there stay refused (`E7004`).
5. Deleting a feature or milestone clears every link to it in the same operation. It never deletes tasks.
6. `dependsOn` is recorded and validated (existing tasks, no self-reference, no cycles), but nothing enforces it yet. D-82 point 4 keeps `blocked` for its later use.

**Update Spec 15:**

- **§1 Task table:** add the five fields with the meanings above. Tasks saved earlier have none of them: read them as null, or `[]` for `dependsOn`.
- **New section, "Features and milestones"** (after §1), with:
  - **Milestone:** `{id, title, body, rank, targetDate?, state: planned|active|done}`. Ordered by `rank` (lower first).
  - **Feature:** `{id, title, body, milestone?, rank, state: planned|active|done}`. `rank` orders features within their milestone, or among features with no milestone.
  - **Storage:** one JSON file each, at `<root>/.solace/strategy/milestones/<id>.json` and `<root>/.solace/strategy/features/<id>.json`, written atomically by the task server, with ids assigned the same way as task ids.
  - Clients use only the API. Agents have no access (Spec 14 §1 rule 4).
- **§4 HTTP:** add these endpoints.

| Request | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /milestones` | All milestones |
| `POST /milestones` `{title, body?, targetDate?, request?}` | Creates a milestone at the end of the order. Uses `request` the same way as `POST /tasks` |
| `PATCH /milestones/{id}` `{title?, body?, rank?, targetDate?, state?}` | Edits it |
| `DELETE /milestones/{id}` | Deletes it and clears `milestone` on every feature and task linked to it |
| `GET /features` | All features |
| `POST /features` `{title, body?, milestone?, request?}` | Creates a feature at the end of its group |
| `PATCH /features/{id}` `{title?, body?, milestone?, rank?, state?}` | Edits it |
| `DELETE /features/{id}` | Deletes it and clears `feature` on every task linked to it |

- `PATCH /tasks/{id}` also accepts `{feature?, milestone?, dependsOn?}`.

- **Errors:** an unknown feature or milestone id, a `dependsOn` naming a missing task or itself, and a `dependsOn` cycle. Each gets the next free `E70xx` code.
- **Events:** add `{milestone}` and `{feature}` in full after every change, and `{removedMilestone: id}` and `{removedFeature: id}`. They go on the root task log, so the `tasks` position in `Last-Event-ID` resumes them. A new connection's replay sends `{milestones: [...]}` and `{features: [...]}` after `{tasks}`. A delete that clears links also sends `{task}` for each changed task.
- **Strategy:** the vision document is left out of this spec. It belongs to the Strategy page work.

**Done when:** D-87 is in `DECISIONS.md`, Spec 15 has the changes above, and the spec's header lists D-87 under **Implements**.
title: Specify the Feature/Milestone store
